title: How to Convert a Diplomat Salary from Hourly to Annual: Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top
description: Understand how to convert a diplomat salary from hourly to annual using 38-hour weeks, 52 weeks, casual loading, and super paid on top. Includes Fair Work rates and tax.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, the annual gross salary is $52,254.88, with super of $6,270.59 paid on top.

faqs.q: Does the casual loading of 25% apply to a diplomat salary?
faqs.a: Yes, if the locally engaged staff member is classified as a casual employee under the Fair Work Act, the employer must pay a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This is set by the National Minimum Wage Order 2026 and applies to award-free employees. For example, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 plus 25%). The loading is not applied to superannuation; super is calculated on the ordinary time earnings.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a diplomat salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation Guarantee contributions are paid on top of the employee's ordinary time earnings at the rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a full-time employee earning $26.44 per hour for 38 hours per week, ordinary time earnings are $1,004.90 per week. Super is $120.59 per week, paid separately by the employer. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830 per year.

faqs.q: What tax applies to a diplomat salary for locally engaged staff?
faqs.a: Locally engaged staff must pay Australian income tax on their earnings. The employer withholds PAYG tax. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. A 2% Medicare levy generally applies. The tax-free threshold is included. The employer must also register with the ATO for PAYG withholding.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Diplomat Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you are offered a **diplomat salary** as a locally engaged staff (LES) member at an embassy or consulate in Australia, your pay must meet Australian workplace standards. This includes the National Minimum Wage, modern award coverage, casual loading, superannuation, and tax withholding. The Fair Work Ombudsman confirms that employees of foreign missions are covered by the Fair Work Act 2009 unless diplomatic immunity applies. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) protocol guidelines also state that LES employment conditions must meet Australian minimum wages, leave, and superannuation requirements.

This guide explains how to convert an hourly diplomat salary to an annual figure, including the 25% casual loading and super paid on top. We assume a standard full-time week of 38 ordinary hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The annual gross salary from an hourly rate is calculated as:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, this becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your diplomat salary is $30.00 per hour, your annual gross is $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This is the base pay before casual loading and before super.

If you are a casual employee, the hourly rate already includes the 25% casual loading. The Fair Work Commission’s National Minimum Wage Order 2026 sets the casual loading at 25% on top of the minimum wage. So if your base rate is $26.44, the casual rate is $33.05. You should never type a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator that expects a base rate; instead, use the base rate and add the loading separately.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Casual loading compensates casual employees for not receiving paid leave. It is paid on top of the base hourly rate. Superannuation Guarantee (SG) contributions, currently 12% of ordinary time earnings, are paid by the employer on top of the total salary. This means super is calculated on the base earnings (including casual loading if applicable) and is not deducted from your pay.

For a diplomat salary, if you are a casual LES, your employer must pay:
- Base hourly rate (e.g., $26.44)
- Plus 25% casual loading ($6.61) → total hourly rate $33.05
- Plus super of 12% on the ordinary time earnings (the base plus loading).

Using the minimum wage example:
- Weekly ordinary earnings (38 hours): $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90
- Annual gross (including loading): $1,255.90 × 52 = $65,306.80
- Super (12% of ordinary earnings): $1,255.90 × 0.12 = $150.71 per week, or $7,836.92 per year, paid on top.

Note that super is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For most diplomat salaries, this cap will not apply.

### Award Coverage for Diplomat Salaries

Not all diplomat salaries are award-free. Many LES roles are covered by the Clerks Award (for clerical and administrative work) or the Miscellaneous Award (for driving, cooking, cleaning, gardening, nanny work). These awards set minimum hourly rates that may be higher than the National Minimum Wage. If you are covered by an award, your employer must pay at least the award rate, plus any applicable loadings (e.g., casual, overtime, penalty rates). The conversion formula remains the same: hourly rate × 38 × 52, but you must use the correct award rate.

For professional or managerial roles not covered by an award, the employee is award-free and the National Minimum Wage applies. The DFAT protocol guidelines confirm that award-free employees receive the National Employment Standards and the National Minimum Wage Order.

### Tax on Your Diplomat Salary

Locally engaged staff must pay Australian income tax. The employer withholds PAYG tax and pays it to the ATO. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. The tax-free threshold is included in the rates above. If you have a HELP debt or are liable for the Medicare levy surcharge, additional amounts may be withheld.

To estimate your take-home pay, subtract the estimated tax and Medicare from your annual gross. For a diplomat salary of $65,306.80 (casual minimum wage example), the tax would be approximately:
- $18,200 tax-free
- $26,800 taxed at 15% = $4,020
- $20,306.80 taxed at 30% = $6,092.04
- Total tax = $10,112.04
- Medicare levy (2% of $65,306.80) = $1,306.14
- Total deductions = $11,418.18
- Net annual pay ≈ $53,888.62

Remember that super is paid on top and not included in your taxable income until you withdraw it.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

Our [timesheet](/) helps you convert your hourly diplomat salary to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Simply enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and check the casual loading box if applicable. The calculator will show your gross pay, super, and estimated tax. For more detailed award rates, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). You can also explore [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) topics.

### Key Takeaways

- A diplomat salary for locally engaged staff must comply with Australian workplace laws.
- Use the formula: hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks to get annual gross.
- Casual loading of 25% is added on top of the base rate for casual employees.
- Superannuation of 12% is paid on top of ordinary time earnings, not deducted.
- Tax is withheld by the employer using the ATO’s PAYG system.
- Always check award coverage – the Clerks Award or Miscellaneous Award may set higher minimums.

For further reading, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) pages. The Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission are the authoritative sources for pay rates.
